headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist by default when Khoj feeds Langflow flows that can write, execute, and exfiltrate.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Khoj reads indexed notes/files and can use web search, while Langflow can ingest uploaded files and chain tools in flows. If Khoj output or retrieved content is passed into Langflow without provenance checks, prompt-like instructions in content can steer downstream flow behavior. This is plausible in default pairings, though not proven by docs alone.
conditions: IF Khoj outputs retrieved text into a Langflow prompt or node input without sanitization
IF Langflow flow nodes treat file or text content as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Add a fixed delimiter and system prompt wrapper between Khoj and Langflow
Strip instruction-like prefixes from retrieved text before passing it onward
Require a human review step for any generated prompt content
Use a provenance tag that Langflow nodes must ignore as instructions
requires-engineering: add schema validation for all inter-agent text handoffs

B_data_leakage.rationale: Khoj touches personal notes and indexed documents, and Langflow reads uploaded files plus stores per-flow credentials while sending data to model providers and arbitrary HTTP services. In a shared workflow, sensitive notes can flow from Khoj into Langflow and then out to third-party APIs by default, creating an exfiltration path with broad blast radius.
conditions: IF a Khoj retrieval result containing personal notes is passed into a Langflow flow
IF that Langflow flow calls an external model provider or HTTP service
mitigations: Disable external HTTP/model nodes for flows handling personal notes
Route only redacted excerpts from Khoj into Langflow
Separate credentials and stores for note-handling flows
Review Langflow flow outputs before sending them externally
requires-engineering: enforce data-class labels on inter-agent transfers

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Khoj is read-only on filesystem, but Langflow can write files, execute shell, spawn subprocesses, and run unsandboxed Python by default. If both are pointed at the same workspace or server-side store, Langflow can overwrite or mutate artifacts that Khoj indexes, creating direct write/read conflict and possible corruption. The pair’s shared-state models make this plausible.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same directory or shared store
IF Langflow flow components write or mutate files that Khoj indexes
mitigations: Place Khoj indexes and Langflow workspaces in separate directories
Disable write-capable Langflow nodes for shared artifacts
Use per-flow service accounts with least privilege
Add file-locking around any shared store
requires-engineering: introduce a read-only mirror for Khoj inputs

D_cascading_error.rationale: Khoj produces retrieved answers from notes and documents, and Langflow is a graph-based orchestrator that can chain multiple agents and tools. If Langflow treats Khoj output as authoritative, downstream nodes may act on unverified facts or citations, causing incorrect actions or propagated errors. This is a default-risk pathway because verification is not described as enabled.
conditions: IF Langflow uses Khoj output as an input to action-taking nodes
IF no verification or cross-check step is inserted between Khoj and downstream tools
mitigations: Insert a verification node before any action-taking step
Require source links for every Khoj-derived claim
Limit Langflow to summarization-only flows for Khoj outputs
Add a human approval gate before external side effects
requires-engineering: implement confidence thresholds for downstream actions

E_compliance.rationale: Khoj is positioned for personal notes and indexed documents, while Langflow stores per-flow credentials and processes flow inputs/intermediate outputs. If regulated or residency-bound data is routed from Khoj into Langflow, retention and residency obligations may diverge across the two systems. The profiles do not specify a concrete jurisdiction mismatch, so this is a policy-gap risk rather than a proven breach.
conditions: IF regulated personal notes or documents are routed from Khoj into Langflow
IF Langflow retention or external API handling differs from the source-data policy
mitigations: Document a shared retention policy for both systems
Exclude regulated data from Langflow flows
Purge intermediate flow outputs after completion
Review where credentials and logs are stored
requires-engineering: map data residency and retention controls end to end
